title: Entrepreneurship Studio: Brand, Product, Sales & Pitch
subtitle: Write the company, the offer, the outreach, and the deck — this month.
description: The founder voice — thesis, brand language, sales script, and a deck you can say out loud. The idea → customer → shipped-product loop lives only in Building Your Own Product.
outcomes: Company written — thesis, offer, outreach, and a spoken pitch

modules.title: Week 1: Pick a problem you can sell this quarter
modules.summary: Stress-test the idea, then write the 90-day outcome and the first customer list.

lessons.title: How to Get and Evaluate Startup Ideas | Startup School
lessons.description: Jared Friedman’s questions you apply to a real idea this week: who already needs this, why you, why now. Pause after each question and answer it for your company.

lessons.title: How to Get Your First Customers | Startup School
lessons.description: The founder sales loop you will run in week 4: list, note, demo, close. Start the spreadsheet of names while you watch.

lessons.title: Assignment 1: Founder Thesis & 90-Day Outcome
lessons.description: Write the company in one sentence, why you are the person to build it, and one leadership outcome that will be true in 90 days.

assignment.brief: Pick a real problem you would spend a year on — not a class project. Leadership here means an observable outcome, not a vibe.
assignment.deliverable: A founder thesis you can say out loud without slides.

fields.label: The company in one sentence
fields.hint: Lead with what you do. No adjectives that a competitor could copy-paste.

fields.label: Why you (founder-market fit)
fields.placeholder: I have lived this problem because…
fields.hint: Specific history beats 'I am passionate about this space.'

fields.label: Leadership outcome in 90 days
fields.hint: Name a result a stranger could check: users, conversations, revenue, a shipped loop — not 'have a better culture.'

fields.label: What you will not do for 90 days
fields.placeholder: I will not hire a sales team / redesign the logo / …
fields.hint: Founders fail by adding work. List the tempting distractions you are cutting.

checklist: A stranger would understand what you do after the first sentence.
The 90-day outcome is observable, not motivational.
You named work you will refuse, not only work you will start.

modules.title: Week 2: Write the offer, then pick one channel
modules.summary: Fill a value proposition, then decide where you will show up weekly.

lessons.title: Value Proposition Canvas (fill this, 5 min)
lessons.description: Osterwalder’s official canvas: jobs, pains, gains vs pain relievers and gain creators. Fill it for your company before you write the brand promise.

lessons.title: PR + Content for Growth | Kat Mañalac & Craig Cannon
lessons.description: How founders actually sell a brand: owned content first, then press. Pause and pick the one platform you will post on this month.

lessons.title: Assignment 2: Brand Promise & Competitor Map
lessons.description: Write the brand promise, pick the first platform you will sell it on, and map three alternatives you refuse to look like.

assignment.brief: Brand is the sentence people repeat when you are not in the room. Competition is who they compare you to instead — including doing nothing.
assignment.deliverable: A one-page brand brief plus a three-player competitor map.

fields.label: Brand promise (one sentence people can repeat)
fields.placeholder: For [who], we are the [category] that [unique outcome].
fields.hint: If it works for a rival after a name swap, it is not a brand yet.

fields.label: Who it is for — and who it is not for
fields.hint: Narrow is a strategy. 'Everyone who wants to be productive' is not.

fields.label: Three alternatives and how you win
fields.placeholder: 1. Status quo / 2. Direct rival / 3. Adjacent tool — and why a user switches.
fields.hint: Include the status quo (doing nothing, Excel, a WhatsApp group). That is usually the real competitor.

fields.label: First platform you will sell the brand on
fields.placeholder: I will show up weekly on … because the buyers already gather there.
fields.hint: Pick one: a community, marketplace, newsletter, or social surface. 'Everywhere' is how brands stay invisible.

checklist: The promise is specific enough to reject customers.
At least one competitor is the status quo, not another startup logo.
You named one platform, not five.

modules.title: Week 3: Product people come back to + 20-user plan
modules.summary: Define the smallest lovable version, then name how 20 people try it.

lessons.title: How to Build Products Users Love | Kevin Hale
lessons.description: Support-driven product: make a few people unconditionally want you to succeed. Write down the support channel you will sit on this month.

lessons.title: Assignment 3: Product Promise & First-Channel Plan
lessons.description: Define the smallest lovable product, the first marketing channel, and how you will get 20 people to try it.

assignment.brief: Marketing cannot rescue a product nobody returns to. Write the product as a job, then pick one channel you will work this month.
assignment.deliverable: A product promise plus a first-channel plan for 20 users.

fields.label: Who + job-to-be-done + smallest lovable version
fields.placeholder: When [situation], [who] wants to [job], so they can [outcome]. The first version only does …
fields.hint: If the first version needs a roadmap to be useful, it is not first.

fields.label: What 'love' looks like in week one
fields.placeholder: They come back / they pay / they text a friend because…
fields.hint: Name a behavior, not a feeling. 'They said it was cool' does not count.

fields.label: First marketing channel and why it fits
fields.placeholder: I will use [channel] because my users already …
fields.hint: Match the channel to where the buyer already spends attention. Paid ads are rarely first.

fields.label: Plan to get the first 20 people to try it
fields.placeholder: Day 1–7: list, messages, places I will show up…
fields.hint: Do things that do not scale. Names, DMs, communities, office hours — not 'viral loop TBD.'

checklist: The first version is small enough to ship this month.
Love is a behavior you can count.
The 20-user plan names real places or people, not a funnel diagram.

modules.title: Week 4: Sales script, deck outline, send the note
modules.summary: Write the spoken pitch, the 10 slides, and one outbound note you would send today.

lessons.title: How to Sell | Tyler Bosmeny
lessons.description: Founders are the first salespeople: prospecting, a short personalized note, listening on the call, and asking for the close. Draft your note while he talks.

lessons.title: How to Pitch Your Seed-Stage Startup | Michael Seibel
lessons.description: A pitch is what you do, who is on the team, traction, insight, market, and the ask — said clearly enough that someone can fund or buy it. Template notes: https://www.ycombinator.com/blog/intro-to-the-yc-seed-deck

lessons.title: Assignment 4: Pitch Deck Outline & First Sales Script
lessons.description: Write the spoken pitch, the 10-slide deck outline, a cold note you would actually send, and where you will sell the brand this week.

assignment.brief: Sales and the deck are the same story told to different rooms. If you cannot say it in two sentences, the slides will not save you.
assignment.deliverable: A spoken pitch, a 10-slide outline, and one outbound note.

fields.label: Spoken pitch (what / who / why now / ask)
fields.placeholder: We do X for Y. The reason this works now is Z. We are asking for…
fields.hint: Two or three sentences a person could repeat after you leave the room.

fields.label: 10-slide pitch deck outline
fields.placeholder:
1. Purpose
2. Problem
3. Solution
4. Why now
5. Market
6. Competition
7. Model
8. Team
9. Traction / plan
10. Ask
fields.hint: One idea per slide. Write the title and the single sentence on the slide — not a paragraph of speaker notes. Use YC’s seed-deck order if you want a default.

fields.label: Cold note to a first customer or partner
fields.placeholder: Subject + 4–6 lines. Personalized. One ask: time this week.
fields.hint: Short, specific, and about them. The only job of this note is a conversation.

fields.label: Where you will sell the brand this week
fields.placeholder: This week I will post / message / show up on [platform] with [artifact].
fields.hint: Name the platform, the artifact (post, listing, thread, demo), and the person you want to reach.

checklist: The spoken pitch does not need a slide to make sense.
Each deck slide is one idea.
The cold note asks for time, not a purchase.
You named one platform and one artifact for this week.
